q1_repeat_categories.answer: Users repeatedly buy from the same categories due to convenience, habit, and the availability of their daily needs, despite facing some issues with product quality and delivery.

q2_exploration_blockers.answer: High prices, poor product quality, and unhelpful customer service are significant blockers that prevent users from exploring new categories, as these issues erode trust and satisfaction.

q3_discovery_channels.answer: Users primarily discover products through search and word of mouth, indicating the importance of search functionality within the app and positive referrals from satisfied customers.

q4_habit_role.answer: Habits play a crucial role in shopping behavior, as users tend to repeatedly purchase from categories that meet their daily and instant needs, highlighting the importance of convenience and reliability.

q5_info_needed.answer: Before trying a new category, users need information about product quality, pricing, delivery times, and return policies to make informed decisions and manage their expectations.

q6_recurring_frustrations.answer: Recurring frustrations include poor product quality, high prices, delivery issues, and unhelpful customer service, which consistently affect user experience across various categories.

q7_experimenting_segments.answer: Segments that are more likely to experiment with new categories are those seeking convenience, variety, and better quality, often driven by word of mouth and the search for solutions to their daily needs.

q8_unmet_needs.answer: Unmet needs consistently emerging across discussions include better product quality, more competitive pricing, reliable customer support, and efficient delivery and return processes, which are fundamental to enhancing user satisfaction and loyalty.
